operations.name: James H. Manning

expected.charges: Federal prosecution under the Espionage Act of 1917 and/or the Sedition Act of 1918 (mass IWW trial in Chicago).
expected.sentence: Five years in prison (Espionage/Sedition Act conviction).

operations.research_note: Original National Civil Liberties Bureau, War-Time Prosecutions and Mob Violence (March 1919), printed pp.34-35, PDF page39, visually inspected. August30,1918 Chicago heading governs the named sentencing groups: J.H.Manning five years; Walter Smith and Roy A.Brown one year. These are imposed sentences, not actual time served or physical admission dates. The nearby Sacramento heading belongs to a different prosecution.
